content.user_title: Improve LLM Prompts With Proven Patterns
content.value_statement: Inconsistent prompts waste time and make AI outputs hard to trust. This skill guides prompt design with reusable patterns, examples, evaluation steps, and optimization workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use few-shot learning, chain-of-thought prompting, templates, and system prompts.
Provides prompt optimization workflows with A/B testing, metrics tracking, and iteration steps.
Includes reusable template patterns for classification, extraction, generation, and transformation tasks.
Offers example datasets for sentiment, classification, summarization, and SQL generation prompts.
Guides prompt versioning, validation, rollback, and comparison workflows.
limitations: It does not connect to a live LLM service without a user-provided client.
It does not guarantee better outputs without representative test cases.
Users must adapt examples for domain safety, privacy, and policy needs.
The optimization script uses simple metrics and a mock client unless extended.

use_cases.title: Build production prompt templates
use_cases.description: Create structured prompts with roles, variables, examples, output formats, and validation rules.

use_cases.title: Evaluate prompt changes
use_cases.description: Compare prompt variants with metrics for accuracy, latency, token usage, and success rate.

use_cases.title: Standardize assistant instructions
use_cases.description: Document system prompts, boundaries, response formats, and quality checks for shared AI workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a prompt goal
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new prompt.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use prompt-engineering-patterns to define a clear task prompt. Goal: [goal]. Audience: [audience]. Required output: [format]. Constraints: [constraints].

prompt_templates.title: Add few-shot examples
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing prompt with demonstrations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the few-shot learning guidance to create three examples for [task]. Include input, ideal output, edge case, and why each example helps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a system prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Create reliable instructions for a specialized assistant.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use system prompt patterns to design an assistant for [role]. Include boundaries, workflow, output format, uncertainty handling, and escalation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize and evaluate a prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the optimization workflow to compare prompt A and prompt B for [task]. Define metrics, test cases, failure modes, and a revision plan.

output_examples.input: Need a better customer support triage prompt.
output_examples.output: A revised structure with role, intake questions, severity labels, escalation rules, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Compare two extraction prompts for reliability.
output: Recommended metrics: field accuracy, missing-value handling, format validity, and response consistency.
Suggested tests: normal records, incomplete records, ambiguous records, and long inputs.
Revision plan: keep the clearer prompt, add edge-case examples, and retest failed cases.

output_examples.input: Create a reusable prompt template for summarization.
output_examples.output: A template outline with task, audience, source text, length limit, tone, required focus areas, and output format.

best_practices: Start with the simplest prompt that can satisfy the task, then add constraints only when needed.
Use representative examples and edge cases when testing prompt changes.
Track prompt versions, evaluation metrics, and known failure modes.
anti_patterns: Do not add complex reasoning steps for simple factual or low-latency tasks.
Do not rely on examples that differ from the target user inputs.
Do not ship prompts without testing format validity and failure cases.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design, test, and refine prompts for reliable LLM applications.

faq.question: Does it run prompts against an LLM automatically?
faq.answer: No. The included script needs a user-provided LLM client or the mock client used in the example.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The patterns are general and can be adapted for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What prompt patterns are covered?
faq.answer: It covers few-shot learning, chain-of-thought prompting, prompt optimization, template systems, and system prompts.

faq.question: Is this skill only for developers?
faq.answer: No. Developers, ML engineers, product teams, and operations teams can use the guidance.

faq.question: What should users provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the task goal, target users, sample inputs, expected outputs, constraints, and failure cases.
